data.description:
## Problem

rebar's explicit post-write maintenance step (`event_commit_git.run_auto_maintenance`) runs `git maintenance run --auto ...` under the store write lock. Git takes `objects/maintenance.lock` before it evaluates any task, and holds it for the whole run. If the process is SIGKILLed while it holds the lock, the lock file stays behind. That can happen when a container is replaced or OOM-killed. Git never expires this lock, and `maintenance run --auto` then exits 0 without doing any work. Store maintenance therefore stops permanently, with no signal.

## Evidence

- Production clone `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets`: a lock dated 2026-09-03 01:36:18 UTC stopped all maintenance until 2026-11-11 (bug `nickelic-lazuline-gonolek`).
- Reproduced on git 2.47.3 inside the MCP container and on git 2.56 locally: with the lock file present, `git maintenance run --auto` and `git maintenance run --task=...` exit 0, print nothing, and do nothing.
- Upstream git confirms the behavior ("If the lock file already exists, then fail silently"). Downstream reports say the same: Abilityai/trinity#4001, buildkite/agent#4453, Bad3r/nixos#581.

## What the parent fix already covers

Bug `nickelic-lazuline-gonolek` removed the main ways the lock got stranded:
- Bounded git children no longer start implicit maintenance.
- The explicit step runs only incremental tasks, which take milliseconds to seconds.
- A timed-out step is reaped as a process group with SIGTERM, so git deletes its own lock.

One window remains: a hard kill that lands during the explicit step itself.

## Why this is separate

Recovery requires rebar to remove a git-owned lock file. Under the mechanism-delta ratchet, that counts as a new `lock` mechanism, and a bug fix may not add one without a decision. Options:
- (a) Reclaim the lock under the write lock when it is older than a staleness bound, as the index.lock reclaim does.
- (b) Clear it at container start, when the old container is known to be gone.
- (c) Detect it and report it through `rebar fsck` or health checks, without removing it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A stranded `objects/maintenance.lock` cannot stop store maintenance permanently, or its presence is reported through a surface an operator reads.
- [ ] A test plants a stale lock and shows that maintenance resumes or that the condition is reported.
data.title: A hard kill during the store's explicit maintenance step strands objects/maintenance.lock and silently stops maintenance
